Guide & about

krillion · THE DIVER’S HANDBOOK

The Daily Dive

Seven prompts. Twenty-five seconds. An ocean of possible answers.

How to playRarity tiersThe AI judgeDaily and practiceAbout this port

How to play

Each dive has seven prompts, such as “Name a type of cheese”. After a three-second preview you have 25 seconds to type one answer that fits. Obvious answers float near the surface. Rare answers sink deep. Every point sinks you ten metres, and 700 points reaches the trench. If an answer doesn’t register (“no echo”), you can keep trying until the clock runs out. Close misspellings get offered as a correction, and you submit again to confirm. Press F for fullscreen.

Rarity tiers

Plankton (10) is the answer everyone blurts out. Too Clever (15) is the “obscure” answer the whole school thought of. Schooler (30) swims with the school. Rare (60) is an uncommon pull. Deep Cut (85) is true obscurity. One in a Krillion (100) is the designated gem at the bottom of the trench. After a dive, open any round in the results to see every prepared answer and its tier.

The AI judge

The prepared answer bank can’t list every valid answer. If you turn on the AI judge in Settings, your browser downloads a small open language model (Qwen2.5 1.5B by default, an 869 MB one-time download; a 278 MB 0.5B model is available but much less accurate) and runs it on your own GPU through WebGPU, using WebLLM. The judge is consulted only when an answer isn’t in the bank. It decides whether the answer fits and roughly how common it is, and it can award up to Rare (60). Deep Cut and One in a Krillion are reserved for curated answers. Answers it accepts are marked. Nothing you type leaves your device. The only network traffic is the one-time download of the library and model weights, which the browser then caches. Small models make mistakes, so treat its rulings as a friendly referee, not an oracle.

Daily and practice

The daily dive uses the same seven prompts for everyone on a given day (New York time), dealt from an offline bank that reshuffles each cycle. You get one daily dive per day, and it extends your streak. Practice dives draw seven random prompts that aren’t in today’s set and never affect your streak. Long streaks unlock new dive buddies in the wardrobe. Your logbook, settings and runs are saved in this browser’s local storage. Use “Export my history” in the logbook to keep a copy.

About this port

This is a single-file, backend-free port of krillion, an independent open-source game released under the MIT license. The pixel ocean, dive buddies, synthesized sound, and the game flow come from that project. The server’s timing, matching and scoring now run inside the page. The VT323 font is included under the SIL Open Font License. This port is independent and is not affiliated with krillion.io or its creator. Without a server there are no global score comparisons: the results chart shows your score on the 0–700 scale.

Quick questions

Does it work offline?

Yes. The whole game is one HTML file. Only the optional AI judge needs a network connection, and only for its first download.

Why was my right answer rejected?

It probably isn’t in the answer bank. Turn on the AI judge, or try a more common spelling.

Do my scores sync across devices?

No. Everything is stored locally in this browser.
